[IMG: /graphics/e0280ddcb295a30b26cbdbf1cfc42504]

sections.normalized_html:

Each of these congruent angles has a measure that is half the measure of the larger bisected angle. So, we have

[MATH: m∠DAC|= (m∠DAB)/(2); = (79^{∘})/(2); = 39.5^{∘}.]

sections.normalized_html:
By the angle addition postulate, we have [MATH: m∠AOC|= m∠AOD − m∠COD; = 90^{∘} − 35^{∘}; = 55^{∘}.]

The bisector of an angle divides the angle into two congruent angles. Therefore, [MATH: m \angle AOB =2 m \angle AOC = 110^\circ.]

Finally, the angle addition postulate gives

[MATH: m∠BOD|= m∠AOB − m∠AOD; = 110^{∘} − 90^{∘}; = 20^{∘}.]

[IMG: /graphics/352d1d1647663efdd0ecf77db9809d58]

sections.normalized_html:
Let [MATH: m \angle FAC=x] and [MATH: m \angle CAG=y.] Then,

[MATH: m \angle GAF=m\angle FAC + m \angle CAG=x+y.]

Since [MATH: \overset{\longrightarrow}{AF}] is the bisector of [MATH: \angle BAC], we have

[MATH: m \angle BAC=2x.]

Since [MATH: \overset{\longrightarrow}{AG}] is the bisector of [MATH: \angle CAD], we have

[MATH: m \angle CAD=2y.]

Finally, since [MATH: \angle BAD] is a straight angle, we obtain:

[MATH: m∠BAC + m∠CAD|= m∠BAD; 2x + 2y|= 180^{∘}; x + y|= 90^{∘}]

Consequently, [MATH: m \angle GAF=x+y=90^\circ.]

Item 11 — Example: Calculating an Unknown Angle Given Two Angle Bisectors

Example Prompt:

[IMG: /graphics/352d1d1647663efdd0ecf77db9809d58]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
[IMG: /graphics/dab7bd4e42ee35a12c2ebbfc1bad3a7a]

Let [MATH: m \angle FAC=x] and [MATH: m \angle CAG=y.] Then,

[MATH: m \angle GAF=m\angle FAC + m \angle CAG=x+y.]

Since [MATH: \overset{\longrightarrow}{AF}] is the bisector of [MATH: \angle BAC], we have

[MATH: m \angle BAC=2x.]

Since [MATH: \overset{\longrightarrow}{AG}] is the bisector of [MATH: \angle CAD], we have

[MATH: m \angle CAD=2y.]

Finally, since [MATH: \angle BAD] is a straight angle, we obtain:

[MATH: m∠BAC + m∠CAD|= m∠BAD; 2x + 2y|= 180^{∘}; x + y|= 90^{∘}]

Consequently, [MATH: m \angle GAF=x+y=90^\circ.]
